why: The answer depends on the source condition for radiation: only an accelerating charge sets up a time-varying magnetic field (and hence a time-varying electric field) that regenerates itself and detaches as a propagating wave, whereas a static charge gives a steady field and a charge moving at constant velocity gives a steady current with no radiation.
note: 'Electromagnetic Waves and Their Characteristics' is the near neighbour, but that topic is about what the wave is like once it exists (transverse, E perpendicular B, speed c); this stem is only about what produces one, which is the Maxwell-theory fact.
